title: Minimum Moves to Make Array Complementary
summary: Given an integer array of even length and a limit, find the minimum moves to replace any integer with a value between 1 and the limit such that the sum of corresponding elements from the start and end of the array is constant.
statement: Given an integer array of even length and a limit, find the minimum moves to replace any integer with a value between 1 and the limit such that the sum of corresponding elements from the start and end of the array is constant.
constraints: nums has even length and every value lies from 1 through limit.
One move replaces one value with any integer in that same range.
Choose one target sum so every mirrored pair nums[i]+nums[n-1-i] equals it, minimizing moves.
hints: For one mirrored pair, cost is two generally, one over a reachable interval, and zero at its current sum.
Encode those cost changes in a difference array over target sums.
Add transitions at 2, 1+min, current sum, current sum+1, limit+max+1; prefix-scan the minimum.
Summing pairwise piecewise costs gives the exact total cost for each target, and the sweep visits every possible target once.
editorial: Summing pairwise piecewise costs gives the exact total cost for each target, and the sweep visits every possible target once.
